title: GJC alerts BIS over suspected gold adulteration, urges jewellers to tighten quality checks - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) over reports of suspected use of Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys to increase the weight of gold jewellery without a corresponding increase in purity, urging jewellers and consumers to remain vigilant.

The industry body said BIS was taking the matter seriously and maintaining close vigilance. However, it cautioned against panic, saying isolated reports should not undermine consumer confidence in the Indian gems and jewellery industry.

Rajesh Rokde, Chairman, GJC, said jewellers must undertake stringent quality control checks on gold procured from manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers to guard against possible adulteration.

He also advised jewellers not to fall prey to offers of unusually low making charges and to prioritise consumer interests and quality assurance.

Consumers, meanwhile, should purchase jewellery only from trusted jewellers, verify hallmark details through the BIS Care App and insist on GST-paid invoices, Rokde said.

He added that any proven case of adulteration or malpractice would be taken up strongly with the appropriate authorities. Strict action should be initiated against those found manufacturing, supplying or using such materials for fraudulent purposes, he said.

Avinash Gupta, Vice Chairman, GJC, said the Indian jewellery industry’s reputation had been built over generations on trust, transparency and quality. Reports of possible malpractice should not be allowed to erode consumer confidence in the sector, he said.

Gupta urged jewellers to strengthen internal quality control mechanisms and ensure complete compliance with BIS hallmarking regulations. Consumers should also obtain proper purchase invoices and verify hallmark credentials before buying jewellery.

GJC has appealed to industry participants and consumers to immediately report instances of suspected adulteration, fraudulent activity or malpractice to the council or directly to BIS so that investigations can be initiated and appropriate action taken.

The council represents over six lakh gem and jewellery businesses across India, including manufacturers, retailers, wholesalers and allied businesses. Its membership spans the gold, silver, platinum, diamond and gemstone segments, covering the industry value chain from bullion to retail.

The developments come amid concerns over the possibility of sophisticated alloying materials being used to compromise the purity of gold jewellery while retaining or increasing its weight.
